title: The Lizard That Jumps from the High Tree
subtitle: Courage and Confidence Must Be Balanced With Wisdom
author: Babi Magil
summary: This proverb teaches that courage is valuable, but confidence must be guided by wisdom. A person should not take dangerous risks simply to prove themselves. True strength comes from knowing both your abilities and your limits.

sections.heading: The Proverb
content: “The lizard that jumps from the high tree says it will praise itself if no one else does.”

sections.heading: Origin & History
content: This proverb is commonly associated with Igbo oral traditions of Nigeria and other West African storytelling cultures.
African proverbs often use animals to teach lessons about human behavior. The lizard represents confidence, bravery, and sometimes pride when a person tries to prove their worth.

sections.heading: Meaning
content: The proverb teaches that people should recognize their own achievements, but they should also be careful not to become arrogant.
The lizard jumping from a high tree shows courage and determination, but it also warns against unnecessary risks taken only to impress others.
A wise person understands the difference between confidence and pride.

sections.heading: Cultural Significance
content: In many African communities, humility is considered a sign of true strength. A person who is capable does not need to constantly prove themselves.
Elders used animal stories to teach young people about bravery, responsibility, and the importance of making wise decisions.

sections.heading: Story
content: Long ago, in a forest village, there lived a small lizard named Chika who wanted everyone to know how brave he was.
The other animals often praised the eagle for flying high and the elephant for its great strength. Chika felt that nobody noticed him.
One day, he climbed to the top of a very tall tree and shouted, 'Today everyone will see how powerful I am!'
The animals gathered below as Chika prepared to jump.
He jumped from the tree and landed safely because lizards had strong bodies and quick movements.
The animals were amazed by his courage, but an old tortoise approached him and said, 'Your bravery is impressive, but remember something important. Do not risk your life just to receive praise.'
Chika understood that courage was not about showing off. True courage was using his abilities wisely.
From that day, he became respected not because he took the biggest risks, but because he knew when and why to act.

sections.heading: Life Lessons
content: Confidence is important, but humility is greater.
Do not take unnecessary risks to impress others.
Know your abilities and limitations.
True courage includes wisdom.
Recognition should come from meaningful actions.

sections.heading: Modern Application
content: This proverb applies to leadership, business, sports, and personal decisions. People should be confident in their abilities but avoid reckless choices made only for attention.
Successful people combine courage with planning and responsibility.
